headline: Nor’easter exposes timbers believed tied to Nantucket’s 1884 Warren Sawyer wreck
dek: Wooden remains surfaced on Nantucket’s south shore during the weekend storm, reviving attention to a schooner wreck that Massachusetts researchers previously linked to the site.
body: A nor’easter that struck Nantucket on Sept. 26 exposed wooden timbers on the island’s south shore, giving residents another look at remains believed to be from the 1884 wreck of the schooner Warren Sawyer, NBC News reported.

Jason Graziadei, editor of Nantucket Current, saw the timbers near the same stretch of beach where fragments appeared in 2022. The newly visible pieces resemble part of a ship’s hull, but their identity has not been conclusively established.

The Warren Sawyer ran aground near Miacomet Beach on Dec. 22, 1884, while carrying cotton and scrap iron from New Orleans to Boston. A Massachusetts Board of Underwater Archaeological Resources review in 2023 said archival, photographic, historical and archaeological evidence made the earlier remains most likely part of that three-masted schooner.

Jascin N. Leonardo Finger of Nantucket’s Maria Mitchell Association told NBC that the newly exposed timbers could belong to the Warren Sawyer but require more research. The shifting sand and surf that reveal old wreckage can also quickly cover it again, leaving the latest find as a new lead for maritime archaeologists rather than a final identification.
author: NorthEast News Desk
seoTitle: Nor’easter exposes possible Warren Sawyer wreck timbers on Nantucket
seoDescription: A nor’easter exposed wooden timbers on Nantucket believed to be linked to the 1884 Warren Sawyer shipwreck, but researchers say more study is needed.
